title: Kernel auto-selection logging: emit chosen kernel + quant mode + shapes for perf attribution
creator: Noah Patel
description:
Problem
- During the FP8/INT8 benchmarking sprint we’re seeing deltas that are hard to explain because we can’t reliably attribute them to kernel choice vs scheduler vs shape distribution.
- Today we can infer *some* choices from Nsight traces, but that doesn’t scale to the full matrix, and it’s easy to miss a mis-selection (e.g., falling back to FP16).

Goal
- For every quantized execution path decision point, emit structured info about:
  1) quant mode (FP16/FP8/INT8 + specific FP8 format if applicable)
  2) chosen kernel identifier / family (e.g., attention kernel variant, GEMM implementation name)
  3) input shapes (minimal set sufficient for perf debugging: seq_len/prefill tokens, decode tokens, batch size, heads, head_dim, hidden_size; plus GEMM m/n/k where available)
  4) phase (prefill vs decode) and op type (attention, GEMM, RMSNorm, etc.)

Non-goals
- Full per-token kernel telemetry.
- Customer-facing logging changes (this is primarily perf-lab / canary / internal debugging, gated behind flags).

Implementation notes
- Must be behind a runtime flag and default-off in production.
- Must have negligible overhead when disabled.
- When enabled, prefer:
  - tracing span attributes for ad-hoc debugging (internal only)
  - structured perf log events (JSON) for ingestion by benchmark-lab / perf-canary

Acceptance criteria
- In a benchmark run (benchmark-lab), the results artifact includes the selected kernel + quant mode + shapes for at least:
  - attention (prefill + decode)
  - GEMM hot path(s) for MLP
- We can detect obvious mis-selection cases via logs alone (e.g., INT8 run selecting FP16 kernel for a specific shape).
- Logging can be toggled by config (flag + optional sampling rate) and is included in the runbook.

Links
- Sprint umbrella: ENG-24810
- Related: ENG-24815 (FP8 prefill regression), ENG-24817 (perf-canary gating)
- Expected code touchpoints: kernel auto-selector, runtime tracing, benchmark log event schema
comments:
2025-10-03 (Yuki Sato): Started digging into current selector codepaths. We have per-op selection in a few places but no uniform schema. Plan is to add a single helper to emit (quant_mode, op, kernel_id, shape_summary, phase) and call it from attention + GEMM selection.

One concern: ‘shape’ is not always present in the same struct across ops; may need a lightweight ShapeSummary struct with optional fields.

2025-10-04 (Noah Patel): +1 on keeping it minimal. For attention, please log (b, seqlen_q, seqlen_kv, n_heads, head_dim). For GEMM log (m,n,k) and whether activation is fused. The main thing is being able to correlate a perf cliff with a kernel_id + a shape bucket.

Also: please ensure we can distinguish prefill vs decode (even if it’s heuristic / callsite-based).

2025-10-06 (Yuki Sato): Implemented tracing span attributes behind flag `--runtime.emit_kernel_selection_spans` (default off). Added callsites in:
- attention kernel selection (prefill + decode paths)
- int8 gemm selection

Next: add structured JSON perf event for benchmark ingestion (so we don’t have to scrape traces).

2025-10-07 (Allison Grant): For dashboard tagging later: please include `kernel_family` and `kernel_id` as separate fields, and a stable `quant_mode` enum string. We’ll want to group by family (e.g., “flash-attn-fp8”) but also drill down to a specific variant.

If you can add GPU capability info (sm version) that’s a bonus, but not required for this ticket.

2025-10-08 (Yuki Sato): Added structured perf log event `kernel_selection` behind `--runtime.emit_perf_log_events`. Payload fields:
- model, op, phase, quant_mode, fp8_format (if applicable)
- kernel_family, kernel_id
- shape: b, seqlen_q, seqlen_kv, heads, head_dim, m, n, k (optional depending on op)

Verified in perf-lab on H100 with benchmark-lab runner: events show up and can be joined by request_id.

Remaining: docs + ensure overhead is zero when disabled (compiled out fast-path).

2025-10-09 (Connor O'Brien): Please make sure this is safe for canary runs. Requirement: default off; only enabled in perf-canary config. Also avoid logging prompt contents; shapes only.

If this lands in runtime-1.18, call out in release notes under “Perf/Benchmarking tooling” not as a user-visible feature.

2025-10-10 (Yuki Sato): Landed + verified. Benchmark-lab artifacts now include kernel selection events; used it to confirm we were incorrectly selecting FP16 kernel for a subset of INT8 shapes (filed follow-up separately / linked to fix PR). Marking done.
